plan: Hal Higdon Intermediate 1, compressed 18->14, shin-adapted, single 20-miler, Italy travel block
design_decisions: Current-fitness gate benchmarked against best-demonstrated recent week (24.5mi, w/c 13-07), not the noisy 8-week average — organic training varies 8.6-29.7mi/wk, average understates real capacity. Confirmed with me 28-07-2026.

long_run_ratio_max is per-week, set to what's realistically achieved with sane training volume, not forced to a uniform 0.32 -- hitting 0.32 at 18-20mi long runs would need ~56-62mi/week total training. Even Higdon's own uncompressed plan never achieves 25-30% (33-50% computed across all 18 weeks). Confirmed with me 28-07-2026.

Higdon's week-9 half marathon dropped -- no slot in the compressed structure, and the 08-08 Percy Sutton 5K already serves as the plan's benchmark race. Also, research (step 4) flagged Higdon's own placement of that half marathon, immediately after a rest day into hard running, as a minor recovery-principle critique.
One 20-miler (week 11) instead of Higdon's two -- no defensible way found to add a second 20 within ~7 weeks of true build+push time without cutting the taper or unsafe long-run spacing.

Compliance floors deliberately traded strictness for realism at my explicit request 28-07-2026: build 0.90->0.95, pre_travel 0.85->0.90 (full control, no travel disruption -- high bar); travel_italy 0.55->0.40, return 0.70->0.55 (travel genuinely limits what's achievable, especially the long run in Italy, which I explicitly do not want to rely on).

REVISION 31-07-2026, confirmed with me: weeks 1-7 (build + pre_travel, full control, no travel disruption) restored to a 5-running-day structure (matching Higdon's own Tue/Wed/Thu/Sat/Sun layout, cross on Monday as an addition not a replacement) and long runs lengthened beyond Higdon's comparable weeks, on the basis that (a) my shin/hamstring symptoms have historically been mild-background-only, never sharp/gait-changing, and are now monitored daily so load can be adjusted reactively rather than pre-emptively cut; (b) research reviewed 31-07-2026 shows elliptical substitution preserves aerobic fitness (~85-95% transfer, null-difference RCT) but does NOT preserve running-specific durability -- eccentric-damage resistance / the repeated-bout effect is movement-specific and doesn't transfer from cross-training, and Boston Marathon race-performance data (PMC12441744) found running sessions/week and quality sessions/week independently predict finish time; bone-stress-injury literature (Warden et al.) supports ~4-5 running days/week as the well-adapted frequency, not a compromise. Net effect: build-phase weekly running total rises from 183mi to ~206mi (+13%) and weeks 1-7 run_days go from mostly-4 to 5; the single 20-miler (week 11, A3) and the 18-miler (week 6, A3) stay exactly as locked -- those are protected regardless. Full parity with Higdon's 588mi 18-week total was explicitly considered and rejected as unsafe: closing that gap fully would require ~55mi/week averages in early build weeks, more than double the current best-demonstrated organic week (24.5mi) and a clear violation of safe week-over-week progression -- flagged as 'something crazy' territory per my own instruction, not attempted. The remaining ~188mi shortfall vs Higdon's total is structural (4 fewer weeks, one 20-miler instead of two, and genuine Italy-travel volume loss that isn't being clawed back) -- not an artifact of over-conservative weighting. Open item, not yet decided: I separately flagged that build/pre_travel long runs should be reassessed for further lengthening -- revisit with real shin-log data from the first 2-3 weeks of the 5-day structure before pushing further, rather than front-loading more now.
